snippet.title: BugSquash - Devlog 2 - Creating a Dynamic Swatting Experience
snippet.description:
The swatter in the BugSquash prototype was very basic. It was the same animation that played on every attack, and it always hit using the same trajectory. The trajectory was also not very realistic, as swatters will typically smack right against the wall.


To improve this experience, I first created a temporary yellow ball as a target in front of the camera that appears when the player is within a certain distance of an object, such as a wall or even a table.

Once this was working, I changed the yellow ball to a “ghost” image of the swatter which would show the calculated strike position of the swatter if the player were to attack.

I then added some variations in the angle that the swatter strikes, and created a custom procedurally generated animation so the swatter moves slightly differently on each swing.

Once I was happy with the animation, I added sound effects when the swatter hits an object, and also ensured that the swatter makes no sound when swinging air. There is now also a new, separate sound when the fly is hit.

Putting it all together, I removed the temporary ghost image to create a more immersive swatting experience.


BugSquash is under active development and is available for Wishlist on Steam https://store.steampowered.com/app/3522470/BugSquash/
You can follow development on martilogames.com or youtube.com/@martilogames
